as_told.title: Ingo Swann remote views Nordics and slave labor on the Moon

plain: Around 1972, the story goes, Ingo Swann, a man trained in remote viewing (trying to see faraway places using only the mind), viewed alien bases on the Moon. Michels mentions it in passing in an episode with the lawyer Danny Sheehan, saying people like Swann would "remote view alien bases on the moon," and he ties it to Swann's book Penetration. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells a much fuller version as something he learned from Swann's account. In his telling, Swann saw tall, "statuesque Nordic people" who looked at him as if to say "You don't belong here" and warned him not to come back. Jorjani says Swann saw these same beings ruling over armies of naked slave labourers on the far side of the Moon. He links the episode to a man called Axelrod, who appears in Swann's story. If true, it would mean someone was living and working on the Moon unseen.
